rationale:
TRIAGE: All three candidates merit close downstream comparison because they split into two endpoint families with different evidence packaging.

- PGS001033 targets a broader but directly aligned EFO (“blood coagulation disease”) with explicit time-to-event phenotyping and provides clean, comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) plus full-model AUROC with conventional covariates. It also has a much larger validation N and multi-ancestry evaluation distribution (even though the selected validation ancestry is European). This makes it a strong anchor candidate for predictive evidence.

- PGS002034 and PGS001826 are sibling scores from the same publication, same reported phenotype (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors”), same training size and validation setup, but different methods/variant counts (LDpred2 with many variants vs penalized regression with few). Their reported performance is partial correlation (partial-r) rather than AUROC/R², which can mislead a single-shot picker if compared naively against AUROC-based reporting in PGS001033. Because they are near-ties on the visible metric (0.0563 vs 0.0562 with overlapping CIs) and differ mainly by model complexity, they should be kept together for head-to-head comparison and for assessing whether the narrower endpoint family is preferable despite less directly comparable metrics.

Keeping all three avoids prematurely favoring (a) the cleaner AUROC-reported broader endpoint (PGS001033) over (b) the narrower-endpoint siblings with different metric type, or vice versa. Uncertainty: Cross-candidate comparability is limited because PGS001033 reports AUROC/R² (PRS-only and full-model) while PGS001826/PGS002034 report partial-r; without a shared metric axis or additional performance fields, the apparent strength/weakness could be an artifact of reporting. Endpoint alignment also differs (broader coagulation-defect TTE vs narrower congenital deficiency), so downstream comparison should explicitly separate “endpoint fidelity to target” from “strength/cleanliness of predictive evidence.” LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All three candidates are direct matches at the broad concept level (coagulation disorders), but none is a clean, high-confidence match for the generic target “blood coagulation disease.” PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (“blood coagulation disease”) and provides PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS R² (0.0578), with only basic covariates; however, its endpoint is a time-to-event UK Biobank pan-trait sparse score with only 1 variant, which domain guidance flags as a framework/sparse-model weakness for external generalization. The other two models (PGS001826, PGS002034) are for a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the target EFO) and report only partial correlation (no AUROC/R²), making them harder to compare and less clearly aligned to the broad target. Given these tradeoffs, PGS001033 is the best-supported direct-match from the visible evidence, but overall evidence quality is limited and endpoint specificity remains a concern. PICK: Keeping the legacy proposal is defensible on the visible evidence. PGS001033 is the only candidate whose trait_efo exactly matches the target concept (“blood coagulation disease”) and it reports directly comparable discrimination/variance metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.634 with CI; PGS-only R² 0.0578; plus full-model AUROC 0.656 with conventional covariates). It also has substantially larger validation N (67,425) and broader evaluation ancestry distribution than the two congenital-deficiency siblings.

PGS002034 and PGS001826 are narrower-endpoint scores (congenital clotting-factor deficiency; different EFO than the target) and only report partial correlation (~0.0563/~0.0562 with overlapping CIs), which is harder to compare head-to-head against AUROC/R² and does not, on its face, provide stronger predictive evidence than PGS001033 across multiple independent axes. Between those two, PGS002034 is a marginal runner-up (near-identical partial-r but much larger variant set), yet neither provides enough endpoint alignment or visibly stronger performance evidence to overturn the direct EFO match and richer performance reporting of PGS001033.

Overall quality remains sub-optimal because PGS001033’s endpoint is a UKB time-to-event “other coagulation defects” pan-trait model and the score is extremely sparse (1 variant), which limits confidence despite the clean metrics. CRITIC: No visible contradiction found with keeping PGS001033 as best among the three. It is the only candidate whose trait_efo exactly matches the target concept (“blood coagulation disease”), and it provides richer, directly interpretable predictive evidence (PGS-only AUROC 0.634 with CI; PGS-only R² 0.0578; plus full-model AUROC 0.656 with conventional covariates) and a much larger validation sample (n=67,425) than the two sibling congenital-deficiency scores (n=19,864 each). PGS001826 and PGS002034 are narrower-endpoint records with a different trait_efo (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency) and only report partial correlation (~0.0562–0.0563, overlapping CIs), which is not visibly stronger evidence nor more directly aligned to the target than PGS001033. The main weakness of PGS001033 (extreme sparsity: variants_number=1; pan-trait UKB TTE context) is already reflected in the low-confidence, sub-optimal outcome, but it is not a concrete reason—on visible evidence—to switch to the narrower, less comparably reported alternatives. The legacy_with_domain_proposal and proposed_pick agree on PGS001033; no basis to revise back to a different legacy choice.

TRIAGE: All three candidates are direct-endpoint Crohn’s disease scores and should be kept for head-to-head comparison.

- PGS004254 deserves close comparison because it reports much stronger apparent discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.72 with tight CI) and an effect size (OR 2.18) in a large EUR validation (n=22,296). However, its reported AUROC is not explicitly PRS-only (no pgs_only_auc shown), so a single-shot picker could be misled if the 0.72 is materially driven by covariates or a particular modeling/endpoint setup; it should be compared carefully against candidates with clean PRS-only reporting.

- PGS001331 and PGS001330 are sibling models from the same UKB snpnet paper with clean PRS-only metrics (pgs_only_auc and pgs_only_r2 provided) and similar covariate sets. They are plausible near-ties and should be compared directly: PGS001331 is slightly stronger on both PRS-only and full-model AUROC and incremental AUROC, while PGS001330 differs by being explicitly time-to-event phenotyping (potential endpoint/horizon mismatch vs standard case-control labels). Keeping both avoids being misled by small metric differences that may reflect phenotype definition rather than true score quality.

Net: shortlist all three to explicitly resolve (i) PRS-only vs full-model metric comparability (PGS004254 vs snpnet siblings) and (ii) phenotype-definition differences within the snpnet siblings (TTE vs non-TTE). Uncertainty: High comparability uncertainty for PGS004254 because the only AUROC shown is labeled full-model and PRS-only fields are null; without PRS-only performance it’s unclear how much of the reported AUROC reflects the score alone versus covariates/packaging. Moderate uncertainty between PGS001330 vs PGS001331 because they are same-family near-ties and differ in phenotype framing (time-to-event vs not), which can shift AUC/incremental AUC without reflecting a universally better PRS. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo aligns; phenotyping_reported is Crohn’s disease for PGS001331 and PGS004254, and a time-to-event Crohn endpoint for PGS001330). PGS001330 and PGS001331 come from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused scores; their PRS-only metrics are modest (PGS-only AUROC ~0.576–0.579; PGS R² ~0.006–0.007). PGS004254 is not from that framework, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with far more variants, and reports stronger discrimination in European evaluation (AUROC 0.72 with basic covariates) plus a strong effect size (OR 2.18), which together support better PRS signal. However, its reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² provided), making cross-model comparability imperfect and preventing a high-confidence selection. PICK: All candidates are direct matches on trait_efo (Crohn disease) and have conventional covariate packaging (age/sex/PCs ± array), so the decision turns mainly on endpoint fidelity nuances and strength/clarity of predictive evidence.

PGS004254 remains the most defensible pick because it shows substantially stronger visible predictive signal in its evaluation: AUROC 0.72 (tight CI 0.70–0.73) and an OR 2.18 (2.05–2.32), with a large European validation sample (n=22,296). It also uses a genome-wide LDpred2-auto construction (744,682 variants), which is consistent with capturing broader polygenic signal than the sparse snpnet siblings.

The main drawback (preventing DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY and keeping confidence moderate) is metric comparability: the record only exposes a full-model AUROC (pgs_only_auc/r2 are null), so we cannot cleanly separate PRS-only discrimination from covariate contribution. However, the covariates listed are standard and similar in spirit to the snpnet records, and the magnitude gap versus PGS001330/PGS001331 (PRS-only AUROC ~0.576–0.579; full-model AUROC ~0.603–0.613) is large enough that the legacy choice remains defensible on multiple independent visible axes (discrimination + effect size + validation N).

Between the snpnet siblings, PGS001331 is the stronger runner-up (slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC/incremental AUROC than PGS001330), while PGS001330 is additionally time-to-event framed, making it a slightly less clean endpoint match to a generic Crohn’s disease target label. CRITIC: No visible contradiction found with keeping PGS004254 as the pick, and the legacy_with_domain_proposal matches the proposed_pick (both select PGS004254), so no revision is warranted.

Visible record check:
- Endpoint alignment: All three candidates are direct Crohn disease matches by trait_efo and trait_reported. PGS001330 is explicitly time-to-event framed, which is a mild endpoint-definition nuance versus the generic target label; PGS001331 and PGS004254 are plain Crohn’s disease.
- Predictive evidence strength: PGS004254 shows much stronger visible discrimination (AUROC 0.72, CI 0.70–0.73) and also reports an effect size (OR 2.18, CI 2.05–2.32) with a large EUR validation (n=22,296). The snpnet siblings have substantially lower AUROC (PGS-only ~0.576–0.579; full-model ~0.603–0.613) in a similarly large validation (n=24,905).
- Metric comparability caveat: For PGS004254, pgs_only_auc/r2 are null and the AUROC is labeled as full-model in the record. This is a real limitation and keeps confidence from being high, but it is not a concrete contradiction, and the covariates listed (age, sex, PCs) are conventional and broadly comparable in spirit to the snpnet records’ covariates (age, sex, PCs ± array). Given the large magnitude gap plus the additional OR evidence, selecting PGS004254 remains defensible on the visible evidence.
- Packaging/leakage: No visible severe packaging red flags (no clinical risk score, biomarkers, treatment variables, or complex EHR summaries listed as covariates) for any candidate.

Alternative check:
- If one were to prioritize clean PRS-only reporting, PGS001331 is the best-supported among the snpnet siblings (slightly higher PRS-only and full-model AUROC than PGS001330). However, the visible performance for PGS001331 is still markedly weaker than PGS004254’s reported AUROC/OR, so there is no better-supported visible alternative that clearly beats PGS004254 overall.

Therefore, keep PGS004254.

TRIAGE: Two main publication families with multiple siblings that are close enough to warrant head-to-head comparison rather than single-shot picking.

1) 2024-12-16 Nat Genet family (PGS004946–PGS004951): these provide PRS-only AUC (univariate) plus delta PRS/residual R²-style increments, which are comparatively clean for isolating PRS contribution even though additional full-model metrics are also present. Within this family, MTAG siblings (PGS004949, PGS004951, PGS004947) show consistently stronger-looking PRS-only AUC/OR than their non-MTAG counterparts in the same validation settings, making them strong contenders. However, endpoint labels differ ("Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy" vs "Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy") and validation ancestries differ (MAE-only vs EUR-only), so keeping multiple siblings avoids being misled by picking the numerically best metric that is actually tied to a different endpoint/validation context.

2) 2024-04-18 Nat Genet family (PGS004861, PGS004862): very large EUR validation (n=347,585) with conventional covariates and straightforward AUROC/OR reporting, but metrics appear to be full-model rather than explicitly PRS-only. These are still worth close comparison because they are direct-endpoint (DCM) and have strong evaluation scale; MTAG (PGS004862) is a plausible near-tie/upgrade over non-MTAG (PGS004861).

Watchlist rationale:
- PGS004950: direct "Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy" EUR evaluation with PRS-only AUC reported, but small validation n=7,761 and an unusually high PRS-only AUPRC relative to other siblings suggests metric-context differences that could mislead a single-shot picker; keep as a plausibly strong but potentially non-comparable candidate.
- PGS004948: non-MTAG sibling in the MAE-evaluated set with weaker-looking PRS-only AUC/OR than its MTAG counterpart (PGS004949) but cleaner as a non-MTAG alternative; keep for robustness/near-tie checks within the same evaluation context. Uncertainty: Comparability is limited by (a) different endpoint phrasing across siblings (DCM vs non-ischemic DCM vs clinical DCM), (b) different evaluation ancestries (EUR-only vs MAE-only) and validation sample sizes, and (c) some candidates reporting primarily full-model AUROC/R² while others provide explicit PRS-only AUC and delta metrics. Because these differences can invert apparent performance, multiple top candidates from each family are shortlisted to prevent over-committing to a single metric type or validation context. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 8 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = dilated cardiomyopathy), with phenotype fields spanning generic DCM, non-ischemic DCM, and clinical DCM. Prioritizing endpoint fidelity and comparable performance within coherent study families: (1) PGS004861 vs PGS004862 are from the same Nat Genet DCM GWAS study family, have identical phenotyping_reported (Dilated cardiomyopathy) and similar basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10) and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL; per domain guidance, the MTAG-enhanced sibling is mildly preferred, and PGS004862 also shows slightly stronger reported metrics (full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; OR 1.76 vs 1.56; R² 0.05 vs 0.048). (2) The 2024-12-16 Nat Genet family (PGS004946–PGS004951) is also coherent and disease-focused but has endpoint shifts (non-ischemic DCM or clinical DCM) and mixed/unclear evaluation ancestry labeling (EVAL: MAE with selected_validation_ancestry 'European, Not reported' for several), making direct comparability to the generic DCM target less clean; additionally, their reported R² values appear to be liability-scale/full-model variants rather than clearly PRS-only, limiting confident ranking by those metrics. Therefore PGS004862 is the best-supported direct-match choice, with moderate confidence due to multiple strong, closely related alternatives and limited PRS-only performance comparability across families. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal (PGS004862) as it remains defensible on multiple visible axes and no alternative is clearly better-supported overall.

Why PGS004862 stays best-supported:
- Direct endpoint alignment: trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are simply “Dilated cardiomyopathy”, matching the target without additional subtype narrowing (vs several 2024-12-16 scores labeled “Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy” or “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy”).
- Strong, straightforward validation evidence at large scale: EUR evaluation with very large validation sample size (n=347,585) and conventional covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10). Reported discrimination is solid (full-model AUROC 0.71) with accompanying effect size (OR 1.76) and R² (0.05). Even though these are not explicitly PRS-only metrics, they are still meaningful predictive evidence given ordinary covariate packaging and consistent reporting within its sibling pair.
- Within-family dominance: compared to its closest like-for-like sibling PGS004861 (same publication, same phenotype/covariates/ancestry), PGS004862 is uniformly stronger on the visible metrics (AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; OR 1.76 vs 1.56; R² 0.05 vs 0.048).

Why not switch to the 2024-12-16 family despite cleaner PRS-only AUC reporting:
- Several of those candidates are not as endpoint-direct to the generic target label (non-ischemic DCM; clinical DCM), and they split across different evaluation contexts (MAE-only vs EUR-only) with much smaller EUR validation for the “clinical DCM” pair (n=7,761).
- The strongest-looking PRS-only AUC among them (e.g., PGS004949 univariate AUC 0.68; OR 1.91) is in the MAE-evaluated non-ischemic DCM setting, making it harder to justify as a clearly better-supported direct-match replacement for a large EUR-evaluated generic DCM score.

Runner-ups:
- PGS004861: same direct endpoint and evaluation setting as the winner, but slightly weaker metrics.
- PGS004949: strong PRS-only AUC/OR, but evaluated in MAE and on “Non-ischemic” DCM.
- PGS004951: strong PRS-only AUC/OR on “Clinical” DCM but much smaller EUR validation (n=7,761), limiting overall support vs the large-scale EUR evaluation of PGS004862. CRITIC: No visible contradiction found with keeping PGS004862, and no alternative is clearly better-supported overall given the record fields.

- Endpoint/label alignment: PGS004862 has trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all as generic “Dilated cardiomyopathy”, matching the target directly. Several 2024-12-16 candidates shift the endpoint label to “Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy” (PGS004946–PGS004949) or “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy” (PGS004950–PGS004951), which is a visible narrowing/definition change relative to the target.

- Validation scale and packaging: PGS004862 is evaluated in EUR with a very large validation sample (n=347,585) and conventional covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10). Nothing in the covariates suggests unusual packaging/leakage.

- Performance evidence (within-family like-for-like): Compared to its closest sibling PGS004861 (same publication family, same phenotype/covariates/ancestry, similar variant count), PGS004862 is uniformly stronger on the visible metrics: full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70, OR 1.76 vs 1.56, R² 0.05 vs 0.048. This supports choosing 004862 over 004861.

- Why not switch to 2024-12-16 family despite PRS-only AUC availability: Those records do provide univariate (PRS-only) AUC and delta R²-style metrics, but they are split across different endpoint labels and different evaluation contexts (many show EVAL: MAE (100%) with selected_validation_ancestry listed as “European, Not reported”, and the EUR-evaluated ‘clinical DCM’ pair has much smaller validation n=7,761). Given these visible context shifts, none of PGS004949/PGS004951/PGS004947/PGS004946 is a clearly better-supported replacement for a large EUR-evaluated generic DCM score.

- Legacy vs proposed: The proposed_pick matches the legacy_with_domain_proposal (PGS004862). There is no visible evidence making the legacy more defensible than the proposed (they are the same), and no better-supported visible alternative that would justify revision.

TRIAGE: Downstream comparison should explicitly cover (a) strongest-looking direct-endpoint predictors even when metrics are full-model packaged, (b) near-tied siblings within the same study family where small metric differences could flip the pick, and (c) “cleaner/alternative” constructions that might look attractive in a single-shot pick but differ in endpoint definition or evaluation context.

Shortlist composition:
- High-performing CHF PheCode family with many near-ties and risk of over-interpreting tiny C-index differences: PGS005074/076/077/078 and PRS-CS counterparts PGS005080/083/084 plus PRS-CSx PGS005085. These share similar covariates (age/sex/PCs) and validation N, making them prime head-to-head candidates.
- Large-scale, direct heart-failure-labeled scores with substantial validation: PGS001790 (PRS-CS-auto; reports PRS-only R2 plus full-model AUROC) and PGS000709 (snpnet multi-PRS; time-to-event C-index/HR). Their metric packaging differs from the CHF PheCode family, so they can mislead if compared naively, but they are too central to omit.
- Recent multi-ancestry-trained HF score with explicit AUROC and additional calibration-type metric: PGS005097 (PRS-CSx; prevalent HF; AUROC + Brier skill). Strong enough to keep in close comparison despite different endpoint framing (prevalent).
- I50-coded HF integration/metaPRS family: PGS004462 (LDpred2) and PGS004532 (RFDiseasemetaPRS). They report ORs without AUC/R2 and have “integration” context that could inflate apparent strength if interpreted as pure PRS performance; still worth direct comparison because endpoint label matches and effect sizes are nontrivial.

Watchlist composition:
- Direct HF but sparse-variant / effect-size-only candidates that can look deceptively strong or simple: PGS003969 (39 SNPs, OR reported, covariates unknown), plus PGS005319 and PGS004598 (context-specific incident HF analyses; HRs reported; not general-population development).
- NPJ Genom Med LDpred2 cluster (PGS005299–PGS005306): multiple closely related models with modest AUROC/R2 and varying dev sample sizes; include as alternatives/controls and to avoid being misled by one split’s performance.
- Remaining members of the CHF PheCode methods paper with lower C-index/OR (PGS005073/075/079/082): keep as plausible alternatives and to ensure the downstream step doesn’t cherry-pick only the top sibling.
- Endpoint-adjacent “congestive HF; nonhypertensive” and “pulmonary heart disease/cor pulmonale” portability scores (PGS001842/PGS002051 and PGS001840/PGS002049): these are not perfectly endpoint-aligned to “heart failure” but could mislead a single-shot picker due to being from a portability-focused paper with consistent covariate handling; keep for explicit endpoint-fidelity checks downstream. Uncertainty: Many candidates report only full-model discrimination (C-index/AUROC) or only effect sizes (OR/HR), with limited PRS-only incremental metrics; downstream comparison will need careful like-for-like framing (endpoint definition: CHF PheCode vs I50 vs generic HF; prevalent vs incident; survival vs case-control) to avoid over-weighting whichever record happens to report the most familiar metric. Several CHF PheCode siblings are extremely close on C-index; the apparent ordering may not be stable without seeing additional validation-ancestry rows or confidence intervals. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: Direct-match candidates for heart failure are present (multiple models with trait_efo=heart failure or congestive heart failure). Among them, PGS005083 is best supported by the visible evidence because it reports the strongest available discrimination metric in this set (C-index 0.7537 in European validation) alongside a relatively strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.455, 95% CI 1.38–1.54), with basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs) and a clear CHF diagnosis endpoint (PheCode 428.1). Competing direct-match models either (a) provide weaker/less informative performance evidence (e.g., PGS000709 C-index 0.635; PGS005097 AUROC 0.72), (b) have missing/unclear covariates and/or only modest effect-size evidence without comparable PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS003969/PGS004532), or (c) are from portability/framework-style UKB scores with limited comparable metrics (e.g., PGS001842/PGS002051 partial-r only). Main limitation: the top metric for PGS005083 is a full-model C-index (not explicitly PRS-only), and several near-clone MVP CHF models (PGS005076/PGS005077/PGS005078/PGS005080/PGS005084) have extremely similar C-index values, making the choice within this cluster not uniquely determined from the provided metadata. PICK: Keep the legacy proposal (PGS005083) as defensible: it is a direct endpoint match (CHF PheCode 428.1; trait_efo congestive heart failure) and sits in the strongest-performing cluster in the candidate list with both (i) top-tier discrimination among the CHF siblings (C-index 0.75368; essentially tied for best in this family) and (ii) one of the strongest reported per-SD effect sizes (OR 1.455, 95% CI 1.38–1.54), with conventional covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs) and clear validation size (n=31,804).

No alternative in the full list shows a clearly better-supported combination across multiple independent visible axes while remaining at least as endpoint-direct. Other direct HF-labeled scores either have materially weaker discrimination (e.g., PGS000709 C-index 0.635; PGS005299–PGS005306 AUROC ~0.57–0.63; PGS005097 AUROC 0.72) or provide only effect sizes without comparable discrimination and with unclear covariates (e.g., PGS004462/PGS004532/PGS003969). The UKB portability CHF scores (PGS001842/PGS002051) report only partial-r in small validation subsets, and context-specific HF scores (PGS004598 breast cancer survivors; PGS005319 medication cohort) are less general-purpose.

Within the MVP CHF methods-paper family, several near-clones are essentially tied on C-index and OR (notably PGS005077/005076/005080/005084). The visible evidence does not justify overturning the legacy pick based on tiny C-index differences alone, so PGS005083 remains the best-supported direct-match selection, with the listed siblings as close runner-ups. CRITIC: No visible contradiction found with keeping PGS005083, and no clearly better-supported alternative emerges from the provided records.

Why PGS005083 remains defensible (vs all candidates shown):
- Endpoint alignment: It is a direct match to the target trait family (trait_efo=congestive heart failure; phenotyping_reported CHF PheCode 428.1). Many other candidates are either adjacent endpoints (cor pulmonale / pulmonary heart disease) or context-specific subcohorts (breast cancer survivors; medication cohort).
- Predictive evidence: Within the large MVP CHF methods-paper cluster, PGS005083 has one of the highest reported discrimination values (C-index 0.7536827) and one of the strongest reported effect sizes (OR 1.455, 95% CI 1.38–1.54) with conventional covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs) and a clear validation N (31,804).
- Packaging/covariates: Nothing visible suggests unusual leakage/packaging beyond standard demographic + PCs; metrics are labeled as full-model C-index, but this same packaging applies across the near-clone siblings, so it does not uniquely disadvantage PGS005083 in-family.

Check against the closest visible alternatives:
- Near-clone MVP CHF siblings: PGS005077 (C-index 0.7535759; OR 1.452), PGS005076 (0.7532491; OR 1.443), PGS005080 (0.7531672; OR 1.44), PGS005084 (0.7527178; OR 1.45). These are essentially tied; none is visibly and consistently superior to PGS005083 across both discrimination and effect size. Therefore there is no concrete basis to overturn the pick.
- Other direct HF-labeled scores show weaker discrimination in the visible metrics: PGS000709 C-index 0.635 (HR 1.08); PGS005097 AUROC 0.72; PGS005299–PGS005306 AUROC ~0.57–0.63.
- Effect-size-only HF/I50 records (PGS004462 OR ~1.16; PGS004532 OR ~1.27; PGS003969 OR 1.28 with covariates unknown) lack comparable discrimination and/or have unclear covariate reporting, so they are not better-supported overall than PGS005083 given what is visible.
- Portability-paper CHF/nonhypertensive scores (PGS001842/PGS002051) report only partial-r in small validation subsets (~20k), which is not stronger visible evidence than the MVP CHF cluster.

Legacy vs proposed_pick: they are the same (PGS005083), and the legacy rationale remains consistent with the visible records. No revision warranted.

TRIAGE: Shortlist focuses on candidates with (a) strongest visible predictive evidence and/or (b) endpoint fidelity to hip OA constructs, while preserving both clean PRS-only reporting and strong full-model/alternative metric reporting for head-to-head comparison.

- PGS000967: Direct hip OA (coxarthrosis) time-to-event endpoint with explicitly reported PGS-only AUROC/R² plus full-model AUROC and incremental AUROC; large UKB training and substantial validation N. Metrics are well-separated (PGS-only vs full model), making it a key anchor for downstream comparison even if its PGS-only AUROC is modest.
- PGS002728: Hip OA context but phenotyping is total hip replacement (proxy for advanced disease). Has an interpretable full-model AUROC with CI and simple covariates (age, sex). Despite lacking PRS-only metrics, it is a strong “direct clinical endpoint/proxy” comparator and could look better/worse depending on how much covariate contribution drives the AUROC—worth explicit head-to-head with cleaner PRS-only candidates.
- PGS004882: Incident hip OA with very large validation N and survival-style reporting (C-index) plus HR. Even though training N is small/atypical and PRS-only metrics aren’t shown, the scale and endpoint framing make it a plausible near-tie contender that could outperform others in practice; also a good check against over-weighting AUROC-only records.
- PGS002763: Hip OA endpoint with a large genome-wide PRS (PRS-CS) and a clear OR with CI in a sizable validation sample. Lacks AUROC/R² but provides strong effect-size evidence and is methodologically distinct from the GWS-only scores, making it a key alternative that could be underestimated by single-metric comparisons.

Watchlist retains candidates that could mislead a single-shot picker (either due to sparse metrics, endpoint/proxy differences, or sibling-method ambiguity) but still plausibly win depending on downstream evaluation criteria:
- PGS002750: Total hip replacement endpoint with OR and richer covariate set; small validation N and no discrimination metrics. Could appear strong via OR but be unstable/less comparable; keep for sensitivity.
- PGS004478 vs PGS004548: Same publication family, same endpoint label (M16 coxarthrosis) and same variant count, but only single-point ORs and covariates listed as unknown. These could be competitive (especially if the integrated/metaPRS approach generalizes), but the sparse reporting and unclear packaging mean they should be compared cautiously rather than selected on OR alone. Uncertainty: Key uncertainties are driven by non-comparable metric types and packaging: (1) several candidates report only OR/HR or only full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-only discrimination, making it unclear how much signal is attributable to the PGS vs covariates; (2) endpoint heterogeneity (incident hip OA vs coxarthrosis TTE vs total hip replacement) can change apparent performance; (3) the 2024 sibling pair (PGS004478/PGS004548) has unknown covariates and minimal performance reporting, so their true standalone PGS performance is unresolved.
